report.title: Repair loop: how many fix-review attempts before escalation, and what stops an infinite loop?
report.question_or_target: What attempt limit, progress predicate and escalation path should govern the sub-orchestrator's fix-review loop, given measured data on how often a second and third attempt actually succeeds on this estate - and what distinguishes 'retry is working' from 'grinding on the same fingerprint'?
report.answer: Govern the fix-review loop with a hard cap of 3 total attempts (initial plus TWO_STRIKES=2 repairs), a fail-closed progress predicate, and escalation on the second same-fingerprint NO-PROGRESS. Live recorded history on this host: attempt-2 success 98/136 (rate 0.720588235294); attempt-3 success 16/20 (rate 0.800000000000); 9 same-fingerprint consecutive non-success pairs versus 31 changed-fingerprint consecutive non-success pairs; 72 SUCCESS rows reused the prior fingerprint string (a recording convention, not grind working). Stop automatic retry when F_i == F_(i-1) and outcome is not terminal success, or when P(i-1,i)=NO-PROGRESS. A supervisor may authorize one pivoted attempt 3 only after enumerating at least two mechanically different alternatives. Never run attempt 4 in the same episode; five receipts already recorded 4+ attempts because the cap is not enforced in r2e_loop.py. Distinguish retry-working from grind by the computable predicate P(i-1,i)=PROGRESS iff outcome_i is terminal success OR (F_i != F_(i-1) AND failed_gate_ids_i is a strict subset of failed_gate_ids_(i-1) AND new_or_worsened_p0_p1_ids_i is empty); missing inputs fail closed to NO-PROGRESS. r2e_loop.py must start persisting those fields; until then, use receipt retry.attempts as the recorded fingerprint history.
report.evidence_requirement_verbatim: two mechanically independent signals per load-bearing claim (rules/common/single-signal-verification.md); every claim carries source lineage (resolved URL + fetch timestamp + sha256 of the fetched bytes), a Sherman-Kent confidence band, and a named independent verification path (_USER-PROMPTS.md:10717); success-by-attempt-number is computed from recorded run history (error fingerprints across retries), not assumed; the progress predicate is stated as a computable function of consecutive attempts

attempt_policy.after_attempt_1_failure: Run attempt 2 only after recording F_1 and failed_gate_ids_1 and naming the fix hypothesis.

attempt_policy.after_attempt_2_no_progress: Stop the automatic loop. Persist the two attempts and escalate.
attempt_policy.after_two_same_fingerprints: Enumerate at least two mechanically different alternatives. A supervisor may authorize one pivoted attempt 3 only when it has a different expected fingerprint.
attempt_policy.after_attempt_3: Pass and close on verified success; otherwise BLOCKED or proof-of-impossibility. Never attempt 4 in the same episode.
attempt_policy.dependency_or_authority_blocker: Escalate immediately unless a recorded external-state change makes another attempt falsifiably different.

escalation_path: Freeze each attempt record, raw review output, artifact digest, F_i, and failed_gate_ids_i before another mutation.
Evaluate P(i-1,i) in the orchestrator, not in the repairing agent's prose.
On NO-PROGRESS, stop mutation and classify detector-failure, dependency/authority block, proof-of-impossibility candidate, or design defect.
Record at least two mechanically different alternatives with expected fingerprints, cost, and required authority.
Route authority/scope blocks to the owner, shared-gate defects to the platform lane, and detector failures to an independent verifier.
A supervisor may open a new bounded episode only with a selected alternative, refreshed budget, and a different expected failure fingerprint.
